title: Certifying and Removing Disparate Impact
abstract: What does it mean for an algorithm to be biased? In U.S. law, unintentional bias is encoded via disparate impact, which occurs when a selection process has widely different outcomes for different groups, even as it appears to be neutral. This legal determination hinges on a definition of a protected class (ethnicity, gender) and an explicit description of the process.

claims.text: Disparate impact in dataset classification can be mathematically linked to the balanced error rate (BER) when predicting protected attributes from non-protected attributes.
A dataset is (1/2 - beta/8)-predictable if and only if it admits disparate impact under the EEOC 80% rule, where beta is the minority selection rate.
The median-based quantile transformation repair algorithm strongly preserves the rank ordering of unprotected attributes within each protected class.
On the Adult Income dataset, full geometric data repair reduces classification utility (1-BER) using SVM from approximately 74% to 72% while eliminating disparate impact.
On the German Credit dataset, full geometric data repair reduces classification utility using SVM from approximately 72% to 50%.
Data repair achieves higher classification accuracy for given fairness levels than Learned Fair Representations and Regularized Logistic Regression on the Adult Income and German Credit datasets.

limitations.text: The proposed repair algorithm operates only on ordered numerical and ordinal attributes, requiring unordered categorical attributes to be removed.
The theoretical BER threshold bound for certifying disparate impact becomes vacuous as the minority class selection rate beta approaches zero.
The formulation of disparate impact is tied specifically to United States legal doctrine and the EEOC 80% rule.
Prior algorithmic fairness approaches modify classifier models or target class labels directly, which reduces accuracy and prevents using arbitrary strong classifiers.

future_work.text: Conducting a systematic study of the relationship between dataset features, classification algorithms, and data repair performance.
Generalizing repair procedures to handle non-numerical attribute types such as unordered categorical data and vector-valued attributes.
Collecting legal frameworks across non-US jurisdictions to investigate whether a single unifying mathematical formulation for algorithmic fairness is possible.

methodologies.name: Geometric Data Repair
methodologies.description: Transforms numerical attributes by linearly interpolating feature values toward a target median quantile distribution across protected classes.
conditions: Partial repair parameter lambda between 0.0 and 1.0

methodologies.name: Combinatorial Data Repair
methodologies.description: Transforms attribute values by shifting their relative rank positions toward the median rank distribution across protected classes.
conditions: Partial repair parameter lambda between 0.0 and 1.0

methodologies.name: Disparate Impact Certification
methodologies.description: Evaluates dataset predictability of protected attributes using Balanced Error Rate optimized via a class-weighted hinge-loss SVM.
